name: Ekom SEO Toolkit
author: itsekomagain

sections.description:
Ekom SEO Toolkit bundles a set of local SEO tools into a single WordPress plugin. Everything runs on your own server: no account to create, no license key to enter, no usage limits.

Site tools (wp-admin):

  • Broken Link Detector — scans posts and pages for dead links
  • Canonical URL Checker — flags canonical tags that don’t point at themselves
  • Image Alt Text Auditor — finds media library images missing alt text
  • Large Image Detector — finds images over 500KB
  • Noindex Page Finder — finds published pages accidentally set to noindex
  • Redirect Manager — 301/302 redirects with smart 404 auto-routing
  • IndexNow & Feed Pings — tells Bing, Yandex, Seznam and Naver about new and updated posts through IndexNow, and adds a WebSub hub to your feeds so feed readers update in seconds (both off until you switch them on)
  • Robots.txt Editor — safely edit the virtual robots.txt output
  • Schema Markup — WebSite, publisher, BlogPosting, author and breadcrumb JSON-LD, so search engines and AI answer engines know what each page is and who wrote it (pauses itself when Yoast, Rank Math or another SEO plugin is active)
  • Scroll Depth Indicator — tracks how far readers scroll per post (no cookies, no personal data)

Editor tools (Gutenberg sidebar):

  • Content Analyzer — word count, keyword density, readability
  • Heading Checker — live heading hierarchy outline
  • Internal Link Checker — internal/external link counts, orphan-post flag in the post list
  • Schema Detector — shows JSON-LD schema present in the post’s block content
  • SEO Previews — Google search and social share card previews, with meta description + Open Graph/Twitter output

A Site Audit dashboard aggregates results from every enabled scanner into one combined report. Every module can be toggled on or off individually from Settings.

Optional paid add-ons: Internal Links, Bulk Meta Editor, 404 Monitor, Schema Pro, AI Visibility and (for WooCommerce stores) Product SEO for WooCommerce. Each is a separate plugin sold through Lemon Squeezy as a one-time purchase. Everything in this free plugin works fully without them; the dashboard lists them in a separate “Paid add-ons” section, hides each one once it is installed, and shows the WooCommerce one only on stores.

Follow development updates on X: https://x.com/itsekomagain

External Services

This plugin can contact the external services below, each used by one optional feature:

Broken link checking (Broken Link Detector module)

This plugin scans your published posts and pages for hyperlinks, then sends HTTP requests to each linked URL to check whether the link is broken (returns a 404, 500, or similar error). This is the core function of the Broken Link Detector module.

What data is sent: An HTTP request to every external URL that appears as a hyperlink in your published post and page content. Links to your own site are checked locally against your database and uploads folder and usually need no request. Results are reused for 24 hours, so the same URL is not requested repeatedly. The request includes a user-agent header (“Ekom SEO Toolkit Broken Link Detector/1.0”) but no personal data, cookies, or authentication credentials.

When data is sent: Only when a broken link scan is triggered — manually from the Broken Links dashboard page, or automatically once a week if the optional weekly scan setting is enabled (disabled by default).

Where requests are sent: Whatever external URLs appear in your own post and page content — third-party sites you have linked to. The plugin does not control these destinations, and the terms of service of those sites apply to the request.

IndexNow (IndexNow & Feed Pings module)

When IndexNow is switched on, the plugin tells participating search engines (Bing, Yandex, Seznam, Naver and others) that a page on your site is new or has changed, so they can crawl it sooner.

What data is sent: Your site’s host name, the IndexNow key this plugin creates for your site (also published at yoursite.com/[key].txt so search engines can verify it), and the public addresses (URLs) of the posts and pages that were published or updated. No personal data, cookies or content is sent.

When data is sent: About a minute after you publish or update a public, indexable post or page, and when you press “Submit all published posts” or “Send waiting pings now” on the module’s page. Off by default.

Where requests are sent: https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow, which shares the URLs with all participating search engines. IndexNow terms, Microsoft privacy statement.

WebSub hub (IndexNow & Feed Pings module)

When WebSub is switched on, the plugin adds a hub link to your RSS and Atom feeds and notifies the hub when a post is published, so feed readers that subscribe through the hub (Feedly, Inoreader and others) receive new posts within seconds.

What data is sent: The address of your site’s main feed and the category feeds of the published post. No personal data.

When data is sent: About a minute after you publish or update a post. Off by default.

Where requests are sent: https://pubsubhubbub.appspot.com/ by default (Google’s public hub), or the hubs you enter in the module’s settings. Google terms, Google privacy policy.

No other module in this plugin makes outbound HTTP requests or transmits data to any external service.
sections.faq:
Does this require an account or license key?

No. Every feature in this plugin runs locally and is free, with no account and no usage limits.

Is there a paid version?

No, this plugin is complete and free, and nothing in it is locked. There are optional paid add-ons, each a separate plugin sold through Lemon Squeezy: Internal Links, Bulk Meta Editor, 404 Monitor, Schema Pro, AI Visibility, and Product SEO for WooCommerce. They are listed under “Paid add-ons” at the bottom of the dashboard; the Add button opens the checkout page in a new tab. An add-on’s card disappears once you install it.

Does any data leave my site?

Only two optional features make outbound requests: the Broken Link Detector’s link check (to URLs that already appear as links in your own content) and IndexNow & Feed Pings (the public addresses of posts you publish, sent only after you switch it on). See External Services below. Nothing else in the plugin contacts an external server.
sections.changelog:
0.1.7

  • Dashboard: the optional paid add-ons now have their own “Paid add-ons” section below the free modules.
  • New module: IndexNow & Feed Pings. Pings IndexNow a minute after a post is published or updated (one batch, no repeat pings for 10 minutes, noindex posts skipped), adds a WebSub hub to your feeds, and keeps a log of the last 50 pings. Off until you switch it on.

0.1.6

  • New look for every admin screen: one header with tabs (Dashboard, Site audit, Settings), square cards, clear status labels.
  • Dashboard: your last Site Audit score, a “Needs attention” list from your modules, and module cards with their status.
  • Site Audit: each scanner shows a pass/warning/problem marker; the last run is remembered for the dashboard.
  • WooCommerce stores see a card for the optional Product SEO add-on.
  • Uninstall now also removes the schema settings, the saved audit and the author profile links.

0.1.5

  • New: Schema Markup module. Adds WebSite, Organization or Person, BlogPosting, author and BreadcrumbList structured data, linked together, on posts, pages and archives. Set your site identity and profile links under Ekom SEO → Schema Markup; authors can add their own profile links on their user profile.
  • Schema Markup and SEO Previews both step aside when Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework is active.

0.1.4

  • Settings and Dashboard now show modules in a grid: three columns on desktop, one on phones.
  • Rounded buttons across all of the plugin’s pages.
  • Fix: the admin menu, dashboard heading, review request and noindex alert email showed an outdated product name.
  • Internal option, table and hook names now use the plugin’s own prefix. Your settings, redirects, scan results and meta descriptions move over automatically on update, and old admin links redirect to the new pages.
  • Developers: add-ons can register their own modules with the ekom_seo_register_modules action.
  • Fix: redirects now match with or without a trailing slash, and work for Arabic and other non-Latin URLs. You can also paste a full URL as the source.
  • Fix: the meta description and social tags are no longer added when Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress or The SEO Framework is active, so pages don’t get two sets.
  • Fix: Scroll Depth kept recording on sites with page caching (it used to stop after about a day), and now counts each page view separately instead of grouping visitors with the same device.
  • Fix: Robots.txt Editor shows WordPress’s own rules in the preview and warns when a real robots.txt file on the server overrides it.
  • Fix: Broken Link Detector no longer reports protocol-relative links, relative links or sites that block automated checks (401, 403, 429) as broken.

0.1.3

  • Translation ready: editor panels, Site Audit, module names and all admin messages can now be translated at translate.wordpress.org.
  • Adds a one-time, dismissible review request on the plugin’s own pages, shown to administrators after a week of use.

0.1.2

  • Editor sidebar redesign: one consistent look across all five panels, clearer score summary, grouped tabs, accessible controls.
  • Site Audit now shows a short summary per scanner (first 5 items, a count of the rest) with a link to the full tool to finish the job.
  • Fix: Keyword Density gauge pointed to the wrong position and its value was clipped.
  • Fix: Schema Detector now finds JSON-LD inside Custom HTML blocks.

0.1.1

  • Fix: Redirect Manager smart 404 matching no longer runs on normal pages, which caused redirect loops.
  • Fix: no longer removes other plugins’ admin notices; plugin notices limited to relevant screens.
  • Fix: redirect type dropdown text was clipped.
  • Broken Link Detector: links to your own site are checked locally instead of over HTTP; each URL is requested once and reused for 24 hours; scans run in short batches so large sites don’t time out; external links use WordPress’s safe HTTP API (private network addresses are refused) and verify SSL certificates.

0.1.0

  • Initial release — all 13 free-core modules (Product SEO/WooCommerce support planned as a separate add-on).
